## Why

Every range rule tried so far (v7.1's AquaMaps P ≥ 0.5, the OBIS P10, hulls, buffers, the regional
effort test in `obis_range_constraint.qmd`) is a **mask**: a cell keeps its turtle or loses it. This
notebook tries the other idea from the 2026-10-06 thread with Tim White, "comparable data based on
effort with strandings and/or survey for the other coasts … so that we can proportionally downweight
Alaska". The suitability stays, scaled by how often turtles are actually encountered per unit of
looking, compared with the US West Coast, where the same North Pacific populations are recorded.

$$
w_{s,r} = \min\left(1,\; \frac{\lambda_{s,r}}{\lambda_{s,\text{ref}}}\right), \qquad
\lambda_{s,r} = \frac{\text{units in region } r \text{ where species } s \text{ was recorded}}{\text{units in region } r \text{ where someone who would have reported it looked}}
$$

- $s$ is a species, $r$ an ecoregion and ref the US West Coast (California Current + Washington/Oregon).
- Each $\lambda$ gets a Jeffreys Beta(½, ½) posterior, so a region with zero records gets an upper
  bound set by its effort rather than a hard zero.
- $w$ is reported two ways. *Central* is the posterior median of the ratio. *Precautionary* is its
  95th percentile, which is generous to Alaska.
- The weight multiplies suitability, so a cell keeps its turtle at a fraction of its value.

The ratio is only fair when the numerator and the denominator come from the **same reporting
channel**, so the notebook builds three lines of evidence from real data. A fourth, strandings, is
mocked up with the Alaska half filled in:

| line | records (numerator) | looking (denominator) | unit |
|---|---|---|---|
| A. surveys | OBIS turtle records | OBIS records from datasets that have recorded a sea turtle anywhere; telemetry and photo-ID excluded | 0.5° block × year |
| B. all records | OBIS + GBIF turtle records (`speciesgrids`) | cells with any marine mammal or sea turtle record | 0.05° cell |
| C. public reports | iNaturalist turtle observations (GBIF API) | iNaturalist marine mammal + sea turtle observations | observation |
| D. strandings | NOAA Alaska Region turtle carcasses and bycatch, 1963–2020 | marine mammal strandings, same region and years | stranding |

```{r}
#| label: setup
librarian::shelf(
  arrow, DBI, dplyr, duckdb, forcats, fs, ggplot2, glue, here, httr2, jsonlite, knitr, purrr, readr,
  readxl, scales, sf, stringr, tibble, tidyr,
  quiet = T)
options(readr.show_col_types = F, knitr.kable.NA = "", dplyr.summarise.inform = F)
source(here("libs/paths.R"))   # dir_raw, dir_big
sf_use_s2(F)
set.seed(42)
dbx <- function(...) invisible(DBI::dbExecute(...))   # quiet in the rendered page

# inputs ----
f_ak      <- glue("{dir_raw}/fisheries.noaa.gov/turtles-alaska/Sea Turtle Sightings & Strandings for MMA Project, 2026_09_23.xlsx")
dir_obis  <- path_expand("~/_big/obis_20250318_parquet/occurrence")   # OBIS full export, 2025-03-18
db_sg     <- path_expand(glue("{dir_big}/speciesgrids_global05.duckdb"))
db_card   <- path_expand("~/_big/sdm/scorecard/published.duckdb")   # obis_range_constraint.qmd: OBIS published ensembles per cell
f_eco_ply <- path_expand(glue("{dir_big}/v8/ply_ecoregions_2025.gpkg"))
f_zc_eco  <- path_expand(glue("{dir_big}/zones/ecoregion_2025-06/global05/zone_cell.parquet"))
f_zc_pa   <- path_expand(glue("{dir_big}/zones/programarea_2026-01/global05/zone_cell.parquet"))
dir_te    <- path_expand(glue("{dir_big}/turtle_encounter"))   # cached extracts
dir_out   <- here("data/turtle_encounter")                      # small tables, committed
dir_create(c(dir_te, dir_out))
stopifnot(all(file_exists(c(f_ak, db_sg, db_card, f_eco_ply, f_zc_eco, f_zc_pa))), dir_exists(dir_obis))

# species ----
d_sp <- tribble(
  ~aphia,  ~sp_key, ~common,         ~sci,
  137205L, "cc",    "Loggerhead",    "Caretta caretta",
  137206L, "cm",    "Green",         "Chelonia mydas",
  137207L, "ei",    "Hawksbill",     "Eretmochelys imbricata",
  137208L, "lk",    "Kemp's ridley", "Lepidochelys kempii",
  137209L, "dc",    "Leatherback",   "Dermochelys coriacea",
  220293L, "lo",    "Olive ridley",  "Lepidochelys olivacea")
FAM_TURTLE <- c("Cheloniidae", "Dermochelyidae")

# weight parameters ----
ECO_REF   <- c("CAC", "WAOR")   # reference: the US West Coast
ECO_AK    <- c("GOA", "EBS", "CBS", "HAR")
SQL_AK    <- paste0("'", ECO_AK, "'", collapse = ", ")
MIN_REF   <- 20L                # fewer reference detections than this -> use the all-turtle rate
PRIOR     <- 0.5                # Jeffreys Beta(1/2, 1/2)
N_DRAW    <- 2e4
UNIT_AGG  <- 10L                # 10 x 10 global05 cells = 0.5 degree blocks

# global05 cell id (1-based, row-major from the north-west corner), as terra::cellFromXY on the cell-id COG
cell_of <- function(lon, lat) {
  col <- pmin(floor((lon + 180) / 0.05), 7199); row <- pmin(floor((90 - lat) / 0.05), 3599)
  as.integer(row * 7200 + col + 1)
}
stopifnot(cell_of(-180, 90) == 1L, cell_of(179.99, -89.99) == 7200L * 3600L)

# ecoregions ----
ply_eco <- st_read(f_eco_ply, quiet = T) |>
  select(region_key, region_name, eco = ecoregion_key, eco_name = ecoregion_name)
d_eco <- st_drop_geometry(ply_eco) |>
  mutate(eco_lbl = glue("{eco_name} ({eco})"))
# a boundary cell belongs to the ecoregion covering most of it (951 cells straddle two)
zc_eco <- read_parquet(f_zc_eco) |>
  arrange(cell_id, desc(pct_covered), zone_key) |>
  distinct(cell_id, .keep_all = T) |>
  transmute(cell_id = as.integer(cell_id), zone_key)
stopifnot(setequal(unique(zc_eco$zone_key), d_eco$eco), !anyDuplicated(zc_eco$cell_id))
f_zc_eco <- glue("{dir_te}/zone_cell_ecoregion_1.parquet")   # one ecoregion per cell, for the SQL below
write_parquet(zc_eco, f_zc_eco)
zc_eco <- rename(zc_eco, eco = zone_key)
```

## The Alaska record: NOAA sightings and strandings, 1963–2020

Jenna Malek (NOAA Alaska Regional Office, stranding co-coordinator) sent these 49 rows to Tim White
on 2026-10-05: the Alaska Region's file for the MMA project. The file is the long-running
Wing/Hodge compilation. NOAA's feature story
[*Sea turtles in Alaska? Yes, we have them far north*](https://www.fisheries.noaa.gov/feature-story/sea-turtles-alaska-yes-we-have-them-far-north)
counts 48 sightings over the same years (19 green, 19 leatherback, 2 loggerhead, 4 olive ridley).
Records from 2020 to the present were requested but have not arrived.

Fixes and flags applied here:

- **Fripo Island (2020):** the longitude is entered as +131.23, so it is negated.
- **Dundas Island, B.C. (1981):** Canadian waters.
- **Cannon Beach (1986):** the coordinates (50.5, −139.75) are far offshore and fall outside US waters.
- **Noyes Island vicinity (1983):** the coordinates (59.0, −134.0) are near Haines, but Noyes
  Island is at about 55.5° N. The record is kept, since either place is in the Gulf of Alaska
  ecoregion.
- **2013 and 2020:** two records have no coordinates.

The ecoregion polygons stop at the outer coast and leave out the Inside Passage, where most of these
records are. So each record goes to the nearest ecoregion within 150 km, and anything south of Dixon
Entrance (54.6° N) counts as Canadian.

```{r}
#| label: ak-records
d_ak <- read_excel(f_ak) |>
  transmute(
    year     = as.integer(Year),
    location = Location,
    species  = species,
    lat      = Lat_dd,
    lon      = if_else(Location == "Fripo Island" & Long_dd > 0, -Long_dd, Long_dd),
    how      = Comments,
    source   = AUTHORITY) |>
  mutate(
    type = case_when(
      str_detect(str_to_lower(how), "carcass|hypoplastron|killed") ~ "carcass / dead",
      str_detect(str_to_lower(how), "netted|live|alive")           ~ "live, in hand",
      .default = "sighting"),
    aphia = d_sp$aphia[match(species, d_sp$sci)])
stopifnot(nrow(d_ak) == 49)

# nearest ecoregion within 150 km: the polygons leave out the Inside Passage and beaches
d_ak <- mutate(d_ak, i = row_number())
pts  <- d_ak |> filter(!is.na(lon)) |> st_as_sf(coords = c("lon", "lat"), crs = 4326, remove = F)
i_near <- st_nearest_feature(pts, ply_eco)
d_ak <- d_ak |>
  left_join(
    tibble(
      i        = pts$i,
      eco_near = ply_eco$eco[i_near],
      km_near  = as.numeric(st_distance(pts, ply_eco[i_near, ], by_element = T)) / 1000),
    by = "i") |>
  mutate(
    eco    = if_else(km_near <= 150 & lat >= 54.6, eco_near, NA_character_),
    status = case_when(
      is.na(lat)  ~ "no coordinates",
      is.na(eco)  ~ "outside US waters",
      .default    = "in Alaska waters"))
write_csv(d_ak, glue("{dir_out}/noaa_ak_turtles_1963-2020.csv"))

d_ak |>
  count(status, eco, species) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = species, values_from = n, values_fill = 0) |>
  kable(caption = "NOAA Alaska Region turtle records by status, ecoregion and species.")
```

Every located Alaska record falls in the Gulf of Alaska ecoregion. The Bering, Chukchi and
Beaufort seas have none in 58 years.

```{r}
#| label: ak-time
#| fig-height: 3.5
d_ak |>
  mutate(decade = 10 * year %/% 10, species = str_replace(species, "^(\\w)\\w+ ", "\\1. ")) |>
  ggplot(aes(decade, fill = type)) +
  geom_bar() +
  facet_wrap(~species, nrow = 1) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "records", fill = NULL, title = "Alaska turtle records per decade") +
  theme_minimal() + theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

Reporting effort is not constant. Most records come from 1976–2002, while the compilation was
actively maintained. The 2003–2020 gap more likely reflects nobody compiling than a lack of turtles,
so the 2020–present request matters.

```{r}
#| label: ak-map
#| fig-height: 5
bb <- st_bbox(c(xmin = -170, xmax = -128, ymin = 50, ymax = 66), crs = 4326)
ggplot() +
  geom_sf(data = st_crop(ply_eco, bb), aes(fill = eco), alpha = 0.25, color = NA) +
  geom_sf(data = filter(pts, !is.na(lon)), aes(shape = type, color = species), size = 2) +
  coord_sf(xlim = bb[c(1, 3)], ylim = bb[c(2, 4)]) +
  labs(fill = "ecoregion", shape = NULL, color = NULL) +
  theme_minimal()
```

Neither OBIS nor GBIF holds any of these records. The OBIS export has no sea turtle north of
48.5° N in the Pacific, and `speciesgrids` (OBIS + GBIF) has none in any Alaska ecoregion (line B).
So the Alaska numerator rests on this file. The comparison is only fair against a lower-48 file
collected the same way, which is line D.

## Line A: surveys (OBIS)

The unit is a 0.5° block in one year. A unit counts as **searched** if it holds any non-telemetry
record from a dataset that has recorded a sea turtle somewhere in the world, meaning the observers
would have written a turtle down. This drops seabird-only programmes, which never record turtles.
The USGS North Pacific Pelagic Seabird Database is one: it has no turtle code and no turtle in its
comments, so its 50 years of Alaska transects cannot count as turtle effort. A unit counts as
**occupied** if it holds a turtle record.

Telemetry is left out, because tags go where the tagged animals go. That means `MachineObservation`,
which also carries placeholder fixes at Seattle (47.5, −122.5), plus any dataset whose name says
telemetry, tracking or photo-ID. The TOPP state-space track summary, filed as `HumanObservation`,
was otherwise most of the "Alaska effort".

```{r}
#| label: obis-extract
f_mega <- glue("{dir_te}/mega_cell_year.parquet")    # birds, mammals, turtles per cell x year x dataset
f_tds  <- glue("{dir_te}/turtle_datasets.parquet")   # datasets with a sea turtle record anywhere
f_dsn  <- glue("{dir_te}/datasets.parquet")          # dataset names
if (!all(file_exists(c(f_mega, f_tds, f_dsn)))) {
  con <- dbConnect(duckdb())
  dbx(con, "SET threads = 10")
  fams <- paste0("'", FAM_TURTLE, "'", collapse = ", ")
  dbx(con, glue("
    CREATE VIEW occ AS SELECT * FROM read_parquet('{dir_obis}/*.parquet', union_by_name = true)
    WHERE NOT COALESCE(absence, false)"))
  dbx(con, glue("
    COPY (SELECT dataset_id, count(*) AS n_turtle FROM occ WHERE family IN ({fams}) GROUP BY 1)
    TO '{f_tds}'"))
  dbx(con, glue("
    COPY (
      SELECT CAST(floor((90 - decimalLatitude) / 0.05) * 7200 + floor((decimalLongitude + 180) / 0.05) + 1 AS BIGINT) AS cell_id,
             date_year, class, family, aphiaid, dataset_id, basisOfRecord, count(*) AS n
      FROM occ
      WHERE decimalLatitude BETWEEN 0 AND 75
        AND (decimalLongitude BETWEEN -180 AND -50 OR decimalLongitude >= 165)
        AND (class IN ('Aves', 'Mammalia') OR family IN ({fams}))
      GROUP BY ALL)
    TO '{f_mega}'"))
  dbx(con, glue("
    COPY (SELECT DISTINCT dataset_id, datasetName, institutionCode FROM occ
          WHERE decimalLatitude BETWEEN 0 AND 75 AND (class IN ('Aves', 'Mammalia') OR family IN ({fams})))
    TO '{f_dsn}'"))
  dbDisconnect(con, shutdown = T)
}

RX_TELEMETRY <- "telemetr|track|satellite|argos|happywhale"   # tags and photo-ID go where the animals are

con <- dbConnect(duckdb())
dbx(con, glue("CREATE TABLE zc_eco AS SELECT * FROM '{f_zc_eco}'"))
dbx(con, glue("
  CREATE TABLE ds AS
  SELECT dataset_id, any_value(datasetName) AS datasetName,
         regexp_matches(lower(COALESCE(any_value(datasetName), '')), '{RX_TELEMETRY}') AS is_tel
  FROM '{f_dsn}' GROUP BY 1"))
dbx(con, glue("
  CREATE TABLE a_rec AS
  SELECT m.*, z.zone_key AS eco, ds.datasetName,
         m.dataset_id IN (SELECT dataset_id FROM '{f_tds}') AS turtle_ds,
         COALESCE(m.family IN ('Cheloniidae', 'Dermochelyidae'), false) AS is_turtle,
         ((cell_id - 1) // 7200 // {UNIT_AGG}) * {7200 %/% UNIT_AGG} + ((cell_id - 1) % 7200) // {UNIT_AGG} AS blk
  FROM '{f_mega}' m JOIN zc_eco z USING (cell_id) LEFT JOIN ds USING (dataset_id)
  WHERE m.basisOfRecord <> 'MachineObservation' AND NOT COALESCE(ds.is_tel, false)"))
n_tel <- dbGetQuery(con, glue("
  SELECT count(*) AS n FROM ds WHERE is_tel AND dataset_id IN (SELECT dataset_id FROM '{f_tds}')"))$n

# searched units per ecoregion, and occupied units per ecoregion x species (+ any turtle)
a_eff <- dbGetQuery(con, "
  SELECT eco, count(DISTINCT (blk, date_year)) AS n, count(DISTINCT dataset_id) AS datasets
  FROM a_rec WHERE turtle_ds GROUP BY eco")
a_det <- dbGetQuery(con, "
  SELECT eco, aphiaid AS aphia, count(DISTINCT (blk, date_year)) AS x
  FROM a_rec WHERE is_turtle AND turtle_ds GROUP BY ALL
  UNION ALL
  SELECT eco, 0 AS aphia, count(DISTINCT (blk, date_year)) AS x
  FROM a_rec WHERE is_turtle AND turtle_ds GROUP BY ALL")
# which surveys make up the Alaska effort
a_ak_ds <- dbGetQuery(con, glue("
  SELECT eco, datasetName, count(DISTINCT (blk, date_year)) AS units, min(date_year) AS y0, max(date_year) AS y1
  FROM a_rec
  WHERE turtle_ds AND eco IN ({SQL_AK})
  GROUP BY ALL ORDER BY eco, units DESC"))
dbDisconnect(con, shutdown = T)

a_ak_ds |>
  kable(caption = glue("Line A: the turtle-reporting surveys behind the Alaska effort (0.5° block-years), after dropping {n_tel} telemetry and photo-ID datasets."))
```

## Line B: all records (OBIS + GBIF)

`speciesgrids` merges OBIS and GBIF records, without dates, onto the same 0.05° grid. Marine mammals
are the effort. Stranding networks, whale watchers and survey crews report mammals and turtles
alike, so a cell with a mammal record is a cell someone was watching. Birds are left out because
eBird dominates them and does not report turtles.

```{r}
#| label: line-b
con_sg <- dbConnect(duckdb())
dbx(con_sg, glue("ATTACH '{db_sg}' AS sg (READ_ONLY)"))
ids <- paste(d_sp$aphia, collapse = ", ")
b_cell <- dbGetQuery(con_sg, glue("
  SELECT s.cell_id, z.zone_key AS eco, s.aphia, s.aphia IN ({ids}) AS is_turtle
  FROM sg.sg_cell s JOIN '{f_zc_eco}' z USING (cell_id)
  WHERE s.class = 'Mammalia' OR s.aphia IN ({ids})"))
dbDisconnect(con_sg, shutdown = T)

# searched units (n) per ecoregion and occupied units (x) per ecoregion x species; aphia 0 = any turtle
count_units <- function(d) {   # d: eco, cell_id, aphia, is_turtle (aphia NA = unidentified turtle)
  list(
    eff = d |> group_by(eco) |> summarize(n = n_distinct(cell_id)),
    det = bind_rows(
      d |> filter(is_turtle, !is.na(aphia)) |> group_by(eco, aphia) |> summarize(x = n_distinct(cell_id)),
      d |> filter(is_turtle) |> group_by(eco) |> summarize(x = n_distinct(cell_id)) |> mutate(aphia = 0L)))
}
b  <- count_units(b_cell)

# variant B+: the NOAA Alaska records added as if they were in GBIF (generous to Alaska)
ak_cells <- d_ak |>
  filter(status == "in Alaska waters") |>
  transmute(cell_id = cell_of(lon, lat), eco, aphia, is_turtle = T)
bp <- count_units(bind_rows(b_cell, ak_cells))

tibble(
  ecoregion = c("any Alaska", ECO_AK),
  `cells, B`  = c(sum(b$eff$n[b$eff$eco %in% ECO_AK]), b$eff$n[match(ECO_AK, b$eff$eco)]),
  `turtle cells, B`  = c(sum(b$det$x[b$det$eco %in% ECO_AK & b$det$aphia == 0]), b$det$x[match(paste(ECO_AK, 0), paste(b$det$eco, b$det$aphia))]),
  `turtle cells, B+` = c(sum(bp$det$x[bp$det$eco %in% ECO_AK & bp$det$aphia == 0]), bp$det$x[match(paste(ECO_AK, 0), paste(bp$det$eco, bp$det$aphia))])) |>
  mutate(across(-ecoregion, ~ coalesce(.x, 0L))) |>
  kable(format.args = list(big.mark = ","), caption = "Line B in Alaska: cells with a marine mammal or turtle record (OBIS + GBIF), and cells with a turtle, without and with the NOAA file.")
```

## Line C: public reports (iNaturalist via GBIF)

The Alaska file is mostly public reports: fishers, beachcombers, newspapers. iNaturalist is the
nearest lower-48 equivalent, so line C counts iNaturalist observations for each Pacific ecoregion.
The ecoregion polygons stop at the outer coast, so each one is buffered by 1° to take in sounds,
passages and beaches, then cut to its stretch of US coast. The query polygon cannot cross the
antimeridian, so this line covers the Gulf of Alaska and the West Coast only.

```{r}
#| label: line-c
f_c <- glue("{dir_out}/inat_counts.csv")
INAT    <- "50c9509d-22c7-4a22-a47d-8c48425ef4a7"
gbif_q  <- function(...) {
  request("https://api.gbif.org/v1/occurrence/search") |>
    req_url_query(..., limit = 0, .multi = "explode") |>
    req_retry(max_tries = 4) |> req_perform() |> resp_body_json()
}
# each ecoregion buffered 1 degree (sounds, passages, beaches), cut to its own stretch of US coast
BOX_C <- list(
  GOA  = c(xmin = -166, xmax = -129.9, ymin = 54.6,  ymax = 62),
  WAOR = c(xmin = -128, xmax = -121,   ymin = 42,    ymax = 48.4),
  CAC  = c(xmin = -126, xmax = -116.5, ymin = 32.53, ymax = 42))
ccw_wkt <- function(e) {   # gbif wants counter-clockwise outer rings
  g <- st_geometry(filter(ply_eco, eco == e)) |> st_union() |> st_buffer(1) |>
    st_intersection(st_as_sfc(st_bbox(BOX_C[[e]], crs = 4326))) |>
    st_simplify(dTolerance = 0.05) |> st_make_valid() |> st_cast("POLYGON")
  g <- g[order(-as.numeric(st_area(g)))][seq_len(min(3, length(g)))]   # the 3 largest parts
  rings <- map(g, function(p) {
    m <- p[[1]]; a <- sum(m[-1, 1] * m[-nrow(m), 2] - m[-nrow(m), 1] * m[-1, 2])   # shoelace (sign = orientation)
    if (a < 0) m <- m[nrow(m):1, ]
    list(m)
  })
  st_as_text(st_multipolygon(rings), digits = 7)
}
if (!file_exists(f_c)) {
  key_sp <- map_int(d_sp$sci, function(x) {
    request("https://api.gbif.org/v1/species/match") |>
      req_url_query(name = x, rank = "SPECIES") |> req_perform() |> resp_body_json() |> pluck("usageKey")
  })
  taxa <- c(
    set_names(as.list(key_sp), d_sp$aphia),
    list(`0` = c(9413L, 5464L)),                          # Cheloniidae + Dermochelyidae
    list(mm = c(733L, 5310L, 5309L, 5308L)))               # Cetacea, Phocidae, Otariidae, Odobenidae
  d_c <- expand_grid(eco = c("CAC", "WAOR", "GOA"), what = names(taxa)) |>
    mutate(x = map2_int(eco, what, function(e, w) {
      wkt <- ccw_wkt(e)
      gbif_q(geometry = wkt, taxonKey = taxa[[w]], datasetKey = INAT, occurrenceStatus = "PRESENT")$count
    }))
  write_csv(d_c, f_c)
}
d_c <- read_csv(f_c)
c_eff <- d_c |> filter(what %in% c("mm", "0")) |> group_by(eco) |> summarize(n = sum(x))
c_det <- d_c |> filter(!what %in% "mm") |> transmute(eco, aphia = as.integer(what), x)
d_c |> pivot_wider(names_from = eco, values_from = x) |>
  mutate(what = recode(what, mm = "marine mammals", `0` = "any sea turtle", !!!set_names(d_sp$common, d_sp$aphia))) |>
  kable(format.args = list(big.mark = ","), caption = "Line C: iNaturalist observations per Pacific ecoregion (1° coastal buffer, US side).")
```

## Encounter rates

```{r}
#| label: rates
# posterior draws of a binomial rate, Jeffreys prior
draw_rate <- function(x, n) rbeta(N_DRAW, PRIOR + x, PRIOR + n - x)

d_rate <- bind_rows(
  list(
    "A. surveys"              = list(a_eff, a_det),
    "B. all records"          = list(b$eff, b$det),
    "B+. all records + NOAA AK" = list(bp$eff, bp$det),
    "C. public reports"       = list(c_eff, c_det)) |>
    imap(function(l, line) {
      d <- expand_grid(eco = l[[1]]$eco, aphia = c(0L, d_sp$aphia)) |>
        left_join(select(l[[1]], eco, n), by = "eco") |>
        left_join(select(l[[2]], eco, aphia, x), by = c("eco", "aphia")) |>
        mutate(x = coalesce(as.integer(x), 0L), n = as.integer(n), line = line)
      # "AK" = all Alaska ecoregions pooled, the fallback for an ecoregion a line never searched
      # (a sum of per-ecoregion units: units never straddle ecoregions on lines A and B)
      bind_rows(d, d |> filter(eco %in% ECO_AK) |> group_by(line, aphia) |>
        summarize(eco = "AK", x = sum(x), n = sum(n), .groups = "drop"))
    })) |>
  left_join(
    bind_rows(select(d_eco, eco, region_key, eco_name), tibble(eco = "AK", region_key = "AK", eco_name = "Alaska, pooled")),
    by = "eco") |>
  mutate(
    sp   = if_else(aphia == 0L, "any sea turtle", d_sp$common[match(aphia, d_sp$aphia)]),
    rate = (x + PRIOR) / (n + 2 * PRIOR),
    lo   = qbeta(0.025, PRIOR + x, PRIOR + n - x),
    hi   = qbeta(0.975, PRIOR + x, PRIOR + n - x))
stopifnot(all(d_rate$x <= d_rate$n))
write_csv(d_rate, glue("{dir_out}/encounter_rates.csv"))
```

```{r}
#| label: rates-plot
#| fig-height: 6
d_rate |>
  filter(aphia == 0L, n > 0, !eco %in% c("PUR", "AK")) |>
  mutate(
    eco_lbl = glue("{eco_name} ({region_key})"),
    group   = case_when(eco %in% ECO_AK ~ "Alaska", eco %in% ECO_REF ~ "reference: West Coast", .default = "other US"),
    eco_lbl = fct_reorder(eco_lbl, as.integer(factor(region_key, c("AK", "PA", "GA", "AT"))), .desc = T)) |>
  ggplot(aes(rate, eco_lbl, color = group)) +
  geom_pointrange(aes(xmin = lo, xmax = hi)) +
  geom_text(aes(x = 2, label = glue("{comma(x)} / {comma(n)}")), hjust = 0, size = 2.6, show.legend = F) +
  scale_x_log10(
    breaks = 10^c(-6, -4, -2, 0), labels = c("0.0001%", "0.01%", "1%", "100%"),
    limits = c(1e-6, 1e3), expand = c(0, 0)) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("Alaska" = "#c0392b", "reference: West Coast" = "#2471a3", "other US" = "grey50")) +
  facet_wrap(~line, ncol = 2) +
  labs(x = "encounter rate, any sea turtle (log scale, 95 % interval)", y = NULL, color = NULL) +
  theme_minimal() + theme(legend.position = "bottom", panel.grid.minor = element_blank())
```

The numbers on the right are occupied over searched units. Zero records against a small number of searched units
leaves a wide interval. The interval narrows only as effort grows, which is the "empty of turtles or
empty of observers" distinction stated as a number.

## The Alaska weights

$w$ compares each Alaska ecoregion with the West Coast, species by species. A species with fewer than
`r MIN_REF` reference detections on a line uses the any-turtle rate instead. Kemp's ridley, the
hawksbill and, on most lines, the loggerhead and olive ridley are recorded too rarely off the West
Coast to pin down a reference rate. That rarity says nothing about Alaska; it only means their
reference is unknown. The any-turtle reference is dominated by green turtles, mostly the resident
San Diego Bay and Long Beach greens on line C.

```{r}
#| label: weights
ref <- d_rate |>
  filter(eco %in% ECO_REF) |>
  group_by(line, aphia, sp) |> summarize(x_ref = sum(x), n_ref = sum(n))

d_w <- d_rate |>
  filter(eco %in% c(ECO_AK, "AK")) |>
  left_join(ref, by = c("line", "aphia", "sp")) |>
  left_join(ref |> filter(aphia == 0L) |> ungroup() |> select(line, x_any = x_ref, n_any = n_ref), by = "line") |>
  left_join(d_rate |> filter(aphia == 0L) |> select(line, eco, x_eco_any = x, n_eco_any = n), by = c("line", "eco")) |>
  mutate(
    pooled = x_ref < MIN_REF,
    x_use  = if_else(pooled, x_eco_any, x),   n_use  = if_else(pooled, n_eco_any, n),
    xr_use = if_else(pooled, x_any, x_ref),   nr_use = if_else(pooled, n_any, n_ref)) |>
  rowwise() |>
  mutate(
    ratio   = list(draw_rate(x_use, n_use) / draw_rate(xr_use, nr_use)),
    w_mid   = min(1, median(ratio)),
    w_prec  = min(1, quantile(ratio, 0.95)[[1]]),
    p_below = mean(ratio < 1)) |>
  ungroup() |>
  select(line, eco, eco_name, aphia, sp, x, n, x_ref, n_ref, pooled, w_mid, w_prec, p_below)
write_csv(d_w, glue("{dir_out}/alaska_weights.csv"))
fmt_w <- function(x) format(signif(x, 2), scientific = F, drop0trailing = T)

d_w |>
  filter(n > 0) |>
  mutate(
    w  = glue("{fmt_w(w_mid)} ({fmt_w(w_prec)}){if_else(pooled, '*', '')}"),
    sp = factor(sp, c("any sea turtle", d_sp$common))) |>
  select(line, eco, sp, w) |>
  arrange(sp) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = sp, values_from = w) |>
  arrange(line, factor(eco, c(ECO_AK, "AK"))) |>
  kable(caption = "Alaska weights relative to the West Coast: central (precautionary 95th percentile). * = too few West Coast records of the species, so the any-turtle rate is used. AK = the four Alaska ecoregions pooled. Ecoregions with no effort on a line are left out.")
```

```{r}
#| label: weights-numbers
#| include: false
nr  <- function(ln, e, what = "n") d_rate |> filter(line == ln, eco == e, aphia == 0L) |> pull(what)
wv  <- function(ln, e, what = "w_mid") d_w |> filter(line == ln, eco == e, aphia == 0L) |> pull(what) |> fmt_w()
```

Read across the lines (any-turtle weights in brackets: central, precautionary):

- **A (surveys)** is effort-matched by design, but OBIS holds almost no turtle-aware survey effort
  in Alaska. All of it is the Lamont-Doherty/LGL seismic cruises of 2004–2008 with
  protected-species observers, `r nr("A. surveys", "AK")` block-years in all against
  `r format(nr("A. surveys", "CAC") + nr("A. surveys", "WAOR"), big.mark = ",")` off the West Coast. So Alaska's zero barely
  constrains anything (pooled Alaska `r wv("A. surveys", "AK")`, `r wv("A. surveys", "AK", "w_prec")`).
  The NOAA AFSC and Marine Mammal Lab cetacean surveys, Platforms of Opportunity and fishery
  observers would make this line count, and they are the survey ask.
- **B (all records)** has `r format(nr("B. all records", "AK"), big.mark = ",")` Alaska cells with a
  marine mammal or turtle record, and not one turtle. Its weights are the smallest
  (`r wv("B. all records", "AK")`, `r wv("B. all records", "AK", "w_prec")`).
- **B+** puts the NOAA records into GBIF as though they had always been there. The Gulf of Alaska
  climbs back toward the West Coast rate (`r wv("B+. all records + NOAA AK", "GOA")`,
  `r wv("B+. all records + NOAA AK", "GOA", "w_prec")`). So line B's Alaska weight measures the
  records' absence from GBIF as much as turtles' absence from Alaska. The NOAA numerator is 58 years
  of every reporting channel, while the mammal denominator is whatever reached GBIF. Because of that
  mismatch, B+ is a generous bound rather than an estimate, and the honest comparison for the NOAA
  file is line D.
- **C (public reports)** is like-for-like on reporting: `r format(nr("C. public reports", "GOA"), big.mark = ",")`
  iNaturalist mammal and turtle observations in the Gulf of Alaska, none of them a turtle, against
  `r format(nr("C. public reports", "CAC") + nr("C. public reports", "WAOR"), big.mark = ",")` on the
  West Coast, of which `r percent(d_rate |> filter(line == "C. public reports", eco %in% ECO_REF, aphia == 0L) |> with(sum(x) / sum(n)), 0.01)`
  are turtles
  (`r wv("C. public reports", "GOA")`, `r wv("C. public reports", "GOA", "w_prec")`). It covers
  roughly the last 15 years, the iNaturalist era, and it misses everything before.

## Line D: strandings, the comparison still missing

The Alaska numerator below is real; the denominators are the data request. For each region and the
same years, the request is turtle carcasses and live strandings, and marine mammal strandings as the
effort proxy: the same beaches, walked by the same networks.

```{r}
#| label: line-d
ak_d <- d_ak |> filter(status == "in Alaska waters", type != "sighting", year >= 1963, year <= 2020)
tibble(
  region                    = c("Alaska (Gulf of Alaska)", "Washington / Oregon", "California", "Gulf of America", "US Atlantic"),
  `turtle strandings`       = c(nrow(ak_d), NA, NA, NA, NA),
  `marine mammal strandings`= NA_integer_,
  source                    = c(
    "NOAA AK Region file (this notebook); MM: AK Region stranding network (Jenna Malek / Mandy Keogh)",
    "NOAA West Coast Region stranding network (turtles + MM)",
    "NOAA West Coast Region stranding network (turtles + MM)",
    "STSSN (sea turtle stranding and salvage network); MM: Southeast Region",
    "STSSN; MM: Greater Atlantic + Southeast Regions")) |>
  kable(caption = glue("Line D, 1963–2020. Alaska: {nrow(ak_d)} turtle carcasses or in-hand animals in 58 years ({round(nrow(ak_d) / 58, 2)} per year)."))
```

Once the table is filled, line D's weight is the same function:
$w = \frac{\text{AK turtle} / \text{AK MM}}{\text{WC turtle} / \text{WC MM}}$, with the Jeffreys
posterior on each rate. The STSSN 10-year summary is public through its
[data application](https://connect.fisheries.noaa.gov/content/cb3f4647-9e4f-4f3d-9edf-e7a87a1feef6/)
(preliminary, Atlantic and Gulf only). The West Coast and Alaska counts have to be requested.

## Applied to the suitability

The weights are applied to the published OBIS ensembles (0–100, the surfaces scored in
`obis_range_constraint.qmd`) on US waters, unthresholded, so that only the downweight shows. The
lines disagree, so each one is applied in turn. An Alaska ecoregion that a line never searched takes
that line's pooled-Alaska weight: the High Arctic on every line, and every ecoregion except the Gulf
of Alaska on line C. The lower 48 keep a weight of 1.

```{r}
#| label: apply
lines_apply <- c("A. surveys", "B. all records", "B+. all records + NOAA AK", "C. public reports")
w_apply <- map_dfr(lines_apply, function(ln) {
  d_l <- filter(d_w, line == ln)
  expand_grid(eco = ECO_AK, aphia = d_sp$aphia) |>
    left_join(d_l |> select(eco, aphia, n, w_mid, w_prec), by = c("eco", "aphia")) |>
    left_join(d_l |> filter(eco == "AK") |> select(aphia, ak_mid = w_mid, ak_prec = w_prec), by = "aphia") |>
    transmute(
      line = ln, eco, aphia, borrowed = coalesce(n, 0L) == 0,
      w_mid  = if_else(borrowed, ak_mid,  w_mid),
      w_prec = if_else(borrowed, ak_prec, w_prec))
})
stopifnot(!anyNA(w_apply$w_mid), !anyNA(w_apply$w_prec))
write_csv(w_apply, glue("{dir_out}/alaska_weights_applied.csv"))

# summed suitability per species x ecoregion x Program Area (the weight is constant within each)
con <- dbConnect(duckdb())
dbx(con, glue("ATTACH '{db_card}' AS card (READ_ONLY)"))
d_suit <- dbGetQuery(con, glue("
  SELECT c.taxon AS aphia, z.zone_key AS eco, p.zone_key AS pa, count(*) AS cells, sum(c.val) AS suit
  FROM card.og_cell c
  JOIN '{f_zc_eco}' z USING (cell_id)
  LEFT JOIN '{f_zc_pa}' p USING (cell_id)
  WHERE c.taxon IN ({ids}) AND c.val >= 1
  GROUP BY ALL"))
n_pa <- dbGetQuery(con, glue("SELECT zone_key AS pa, count(*) AS n_cell FROM '{f_zc_pa}' GROUP BY 1"))
dbDisconnect(con, shutdown = T)

# every (line, weight) applied to the same table; "unweighted" = w of 1 everywhere
d_suit_w <- bind_rows(
  d_suit |> mutate(line = "unweighted", weight = "none", w = 1),
  expand_grid(line = lines_apply, weight = c("central", "precautionary")) |>
    pmap_dfr(function(line, weight) {
      wk <- if (weight == "central") "w_mid" else "w_prec"
      d_suit |>
        left_join(w_apply |> filter(line == !!line) |> select(eco, aphia, w = all_of(wk)), by = c("eco", "aphia")) |>
        mutate(line = line, weight = weight, w = coalesce(w, 1))
    })) |>
  mutate(suit_w = suit * w)

d_share <- d_suit_w |>
  group_by(line, weight, aphia) |>
  summarize(ak_share = sum(suit_w[eco %in% ECO_AK]) / sum(suit_w)) |>
  ungroup() |>
  left_join(select(d_sp, aphia, common), by = "aphia")
write_csv(d_share, glue("{dir_out}/alaska_share.csv"))
d_share |>
  mutate(
    col = if_else(line == "unweighted", "unweighted", glue("{str_sub(line, 1, 2)} {str_sub(weight, 1, 4)}.")),
    col = str_replace(col, "\\. ", " "),
    val = percent(ak_share, 0.01)) |>
  select(species = common, col, val) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = col, values_from = val) |>
  kable(caption = "Alaska's share of each species' summed suitability in US waters (OBIS published ensembles), unweighted and under each line's weight (cent. = central, prec. = precautionary).")
```

```{r}
#| label: apply-pa
#| fig-height: 8
d_pa <- d_suit_w |>
  filter(!is.na(pa)) |>
  group_by(line, weight, pa) |>
  summarize(suit_w = sum(suit_w)) |>
  ungroup() |>
  left_join(n_pa, by = "pa") |>
  mutate(per_cell = suit_w / n_cell)
write_csv(d_pa, glue("{dir_out}/programarea_suitability.csv"))

pa_order <- d_pa |> filter(line == "unweighted") |> arrange(per_cell) |> pull(pa)
d_pa |>
  filter(line != "unweighted") |>
  left_join(d_pa |> filter(line == "unweighted") |> select(pa, unweighted = per_cell), by = "pa") |>
  mutate(pa = factor(pa, pa_order), weight = factor(weight, c("precautionary", "central"))) |>
  ggplot(aes(y = pa)) +
  geom_col(data = \(d) distinct(d, line, pa, unweighted), aes(x = unweighted), fill = "grey85") +
  geom_point(aes(x = per_cell, color = weight), size = 2) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c(precautionary = "#f5b041", central = "#c0392b")) +
  facet_wrap(~line, nrow = 1) +
  labs(
    x = "summed suitability of the six turtles per cell (bars: unweighted)", y = "Program Area", color = NULL,
    title = "Program Areas, turtle suitability before and after the Alaska weight") +
  theme_minimal() + theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

## What this does and does not show

So far, any-turtle weights for Alaska pooled (central, precautionary):

- **Lines with real Alaska effort agree that turtles are rarer there per unit of looking.**
  All records (B) gives `r wv("B. all records", "AK")`, `r wv("B. all records", "AK", "w_prec")`,
  and iNaturalist (C) gives `r wv("C. public reports", "AK")`, `r wv("C. public reports", "AK", "w_prec")`.
  The Gulf of Alaska's share of US turtle suitability falls by one to two orders of magnitude.
- **Folding in the NOAA records (B+) is the generous bound.** It gives `r wv("B+. all records + NOAA AK", "AK")`,
  `r wv("B+. all records + NOAA AK", "AK", "w_prec")`, and the Gulf of Alaska alone sits near half the
  West Coast rate. The truth for the NOAA file is somewhere between B and B+, and line D is the test
  that would place it.
- **OBIS surveys (A) cannot tell yet.** OBIS has `r nr("A. surveys", "AK")` turtle-aware Alaska
  block-years, so the zero there is not yet evidence.

- **The rule.** One multiplicative weight per species × ecoregion, from occupied over searched units,
  relative to the West Coast. Nothing is masked. Critical habitat and the lower 48 are untouched, and
  a single Alaska record cannot flip a cell on or off. The weight shrinks only as fast as the Alaska
  effort justifies.
- **The answer depends on the reporting channel.** Surveys (A) and public reports (C) are
  like-for-like. All records (B) is not, unless the NOAA file is held against an equivalent lower-48
  file, and B+ shows how far that moves things. Line D, strandings normalized by marine mammal
  strandings, is the like-for-like test for the NOAA file and needs the requested counts.
- **The effort definition carries the result, as it did in the regional test.** Seabird-only surveys
  (NPPSD and much of OBIS's Alaska avifauna) are excluded because they never record turtles.
  Counting them would shrink the Alaska weights a great deal without justification.
- **Season is ignored.** Alaska greens are reported mostly October–December and leatherbacks
  July–August (NOAA). An annual weight is the right scale for an annual score, but a seasonal
  product would need the same table by month.
- **Time is ignored on lines B and C**, and line A pools 1950s–2020s. Restricting to 1990 on could be
  checked.
- **Generalising.** The same function gives a weight for every species × ecoregion against that
  species' best-recorded US region, which would make this a candidate rule for the national score.
  If adopted it belongs in msens (`encounter_weight()`) with fixtures: zero detections, the pooled
  fallback, the cap at 1.

### Asks

1. Jenna Malek: Alaska marine mammal strandings per year, 1963–2020 (line D denominator), and the
   2020–present turtle records.
2. NOAA West Coast Region: turtle and marine mammal strandings per year by state.
3. STSSN: annual turtle strandings by state (the data application covers the latest 10 years), plus
   Southeast and Greater Atlantic marine mammal strandings.
4. Survey effort that records turtles in Alaska. Candidates: NOAA AFSC / Marine Mammal Laboratory
   cetacean surveys, Platforms of Opportunity, and the North Pacific Groundfish Observer Program,
   whose turtle bycatch per observed haul sets against the West Coast observer programs. Any of them
   would turn line A from "not searched" into evidence.
5. Lance Garrison (SEFSC on-effort database, already requested by Tim): on-effort turtle sightings
   per km surveyed, for the same weight in the Gulf and Atlantic if the rule goes national.
